$comment: VENDORED MITRE CWE catalogue. CSAF requires a weakness NAME and version for every cwes[] entry, and every CWE source here (CISA KEV, monitor/ruleId-cwe.json) carries the id alone. NOT fetched at run time — the unpinned-fetch gate forbids it, and a catalogue that shifts under a published document silently re-dates evidence. Regenerate deliberately and bump `version`. CWE used under the MITRE CWE Terms of Use; attribution required.
csafTestNote: Everything below exists to satisfy named CSAF 2.1 tests, quoted from csaf-v2.1-csd02: 6.1.11 (MANDATORY) 'For each CWE it MUST be tested that the given CWE exists and is valid in the version provided. Any id that refers to a CWE Category or View MUST fail the test.' 6.2.23 the CWE must not be deprecated in the given version. 6.2.24 the LATEST CWE version available at the last revision must be used — so a stale vendored catalogue fails this test, which is why `version` is here and why regeneration is deliberate. 6.2.25 the mapping must be allowed, which the spec states as 'the two usage states Allowed and Allowed-with-Review' — Discouraged and Prohibited both fail it. 6.2.26 the mapping must be allowed WITHOUT review, so Allowed-with-Review fails it; that test exists to TRIGGER a review, not to forbid the mapping.
categoriesNote: Categories and Views are recorded so a refused citation can be NAMED. They must never reach cwes[] — mandatory test 6.1.11. CISA KEV cites 8 categories across 62 of its 1,676 records.
rejectedNote: MITRE publishes these names and CSAF 2.1 CANNOT carry them: the cwes[].name pattern ^[^\s\-_.](.*[^\s\-_.])?$ forbids a leading or trailing space, hyphen, underscore or period. Exactly one weakness is affected and MITRE grades it Usage: Allowed at Variant level — a name the CWE specification recommends for mapping and the CSAF schema forbids. Verified 2026-08-26 still present at the CSAF v2.1 LATEST stage, not only CSD02. Reported upstream rather than rewritten: 6.1.11's own example fails a cwes[] entry whose name does not match the catalogue, so inventing one breaks a mandatory test as well as being a fabrication.
